chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Buying his mother's ukulele for 25 cents a week
summary: His mother sold him the ukulele for half its price, and Ashton Murray tuned it and showed him chords.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: So I said... Well, I saw this ukelele. So I asked Ma, I said, 'What did you do with that ukelele?' She said, 'I'm not doin' nothin' with it.' [INAUDIBLE SENTENCE] I said, 'Why don't you give it to me.' She said, 'I'm not goin' to give it to you.' She said, 'I'll sell it to you.' I said, 'What do you want?' She said, 'I paid out fifteen dollars for it.' She said, 'I'll sell it to you.' I said, 'What you want?' She said, 'What you giving?' I said, 'I ain't got nothin' to give.' She said, 'Well, I'll let you have it, but you got to pay me something.' I said, 'What you want?' She said, 'Pay me half of what I paid.' Half of $15 is what? $7.50. I said, 'All right.' She said, 'Well, how you gonna pay me?' -- she was putting me on. She said, 'Give me fifty cents a week.' I says, 'Yeah?' 'Yes, that's right.' I said, 'I'll give you a quarter a week.' That's (?) money, you know what...
When you said fifty cents a week, that meant I'd have to pound a whole lot of brick, and I'd have to sell some papers...
That's right! That's half of your fun.

So she said, "Okay, give me 25 cents a week." And I got that ukelele. And I made a beeline to Ashton's house, and knocked on the door. His aunt was very (?). She said, "What do you want?" They were sophisticated, nice and reserved mulatto people. So you'd go through that again. It was hurtin' for me to go in there and ask them for anything. I said, "Is Ashton there?" She said, "What do you want with Ashton?" I guess she had seen me out there playin' with them little girls, talkin' trash, because I was a smart-aleck even then. "What you want with Ashton?" I said, "I want him to tune my ukelele." "Well, he won't be here until after school. Then we have to go somewhere. You can come back later." I said, "Okay."

So I finally caught Ashton, and then Ashton tuned that guitar...that ukelele for me, and he showed me a couple of chords. And I said, "Well, I (?) Ashton." Herman Henderson could play it better than Ashton. So I go... Between Herman Henderson and Ashton, I'm learning the...
